Issues.Title: HwndHost disposed while connected to a window is never collected: HwndSource keeps its keyboard input site
Issues.Body:
## Description

If an `HwndHost` is disposed while it is still in a window's visual tree, and then removed from the tree, the window's `HwndSource` keeps the host's `HwndSourceKeyboardInputSite` in its keyboard sink list for as long as the window lives. The host and everything it references can never be collected. In an application, the window is usually the main window, so every host torn down in that order leaks.

This affects every `HwndHost` subclass: `WindowsFormsHost`, the WPF `WebBrowser`, WebView2's WPF control and custom hosts. Disposing a host before detaching it is the natural order when a view is closed. For example, a document view disposes its browser when the document closes, and the docking framework detaches the view afterwards.

## Cause

In `HwndHost.cs`, only `OnSourceChanged` unregisters the keyboard input site:

```csharp
IKeyboardInputSite keyboardInputSite = ((IKeyboardInputSink)this).KeyboardInputSite;
if (keyboardInputSite != null)
{
    ((IKeyboardInputSink)this).KeyboardInputSite = null;
    keyboardInputSite.Unregister();
}
```

`Dispose(bool disposing)` removes the `SourceChanged` handler (`PresentationSource.RemoveSourceChangedHandler(this, OnSourceChanged)`) but does not unregister the site. After disposal, removing the host from the tree no longer reaches `OnSourceChanged`, so the site is never unregistered. The `IKeyboardInputSink.KeyboardInputSite` documentation says the site "should be set to null before disposal", but `HwndHost.Dispose` does not do that itself.


### Reproduction Steps

A minimal WPF app with no package references is attached (`HwndHostKeyboardSiteRetentionRepro`). It hosts a one-window `HwndHost` (a Win32 `STATIC` child) in a window that stays open, tears it down, forces a full GC, and counts survivors through `WeakReference`:

```csharp
var host = new NativeHost();                 // HwndHost creating a STATIC child window
window.Content = new Grid { Children = { host } };
Pump();                                      // host is now registered as a keyboard input sink

host.Dispose();                              // dispose while still connected...
window.Content = null;                       // ...then detach
Pump();
// force full GC: host survives
```

Run it with `dotnet run -c Debug`, or with `--auto` to print the result without a message box.

### Expected behavior

The host is collected after it is disposed and removed from the tree, whatever the order. `HwndHost.Dispose` should unregister its keyboard input site, as `OnSourceChanged` does.

### Actual behavior

Three cycles of each order, with the window kept open:

```
Surviving hosts after each cycle (3 cycles, window kept open):
  RemoveThenDispose                      0 -> 0 -> 0   (entries left in HwndSource keyboard-site list: 0)
  DisposeThenRemove                      1 -> 2 -> 3   (entries left in HwndSource keyboard-site list: 3)
  UnregisterSiteThenDisposeThenRemove    0 -> 0 -> 0   (entries left in HwndSource keyboard-site list: 0)
```

The retention path is `HwndSource._keyboardInputSinkChildren` → `HwndSourceKeyboardInputSite` → host. In a larger application we also confirmed this path with `dotnet-dump gcroot` for WebView2's WPF control.

### Regression?

Not known. Not tested on .NET Framework.

### Known Workarounds

Unregister the site before disposing:

```csharp
((IKeyboardInputSink)host).KeyboardInputSite?.Unregister();
host.Dispose();
```

Alternatively, remove the host from the tree before disposing it.

### Impact

_No response_

### Configuration

- .NET 10.0.13 (`net10.0-windows`, `UseWPF`)
- Windows 11, build 10.0.26200, x64
- Not specific to a configuration, as far as known



### Other information

A November 2021 comment on MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback#1633 suspected `HwndSourceKeyboardInputSite` was keeping WebView2's WPF control alive after `Dispose()`. That issue was closed for an unrelated WinUI fix, and we found no dotnet/wpf issue for it.

A possible fix is to unregister the site in `HwndHost.Dispose(bool disposing)` (when `disposing` is true), using the same code as `OnSourceChanged`.

Issues.Title: Restore WPF Clipboard compatibility and native EMF support
Issues.Body:
Fixes #11968
Fixes #11986

## Summary

This change restores established .NET 9 behavior for WPF Clipboard APIs after the move to the shared OLE implementation in `System.Private.Windows.Core`. It also adds comprehensive compatibility coverage for the public Clipboard APIs and restores native enhanced-metafile support.

## Compatibility fixes

- Return an OLE-backed data object from `Clipboard.GetDataObject()` so Windows-generated formats and delayed rendering remain observable.
- Restore native format checks for `Contains*`, including MTA-safe behavior and Windows-synthesized formats.
- Restore ANSI `Text` to `UnicodeText` Clipboard conversion.
- Restore WPF-specific `BitmapSource` format mappings without exposing them from WinForms.
- Preserve existing `Clear`, `Flush`, `IsCurrent`, and `SetDataObject` ownership semantics.
- Retry transient `CLIPBRD_E_CANT_OPEN` failures when retrieving platform-specific bitmap and EMF data.

## Enhanced metafile support

- Opt WPF into native `TYMED_ENHMF` rendering and retrieval.
- Support both `Metafile` and stream-backed EMF payloads.
- Correctly assign native EMF handles to returned `STGMEDIUM` values.
- Copy native handles before releasing the source medium.
- Preserve caller ownership and source-object validity.
- Support delayed rendering, `Flush`, and `copy: true`.
- Return independently disposable results from repeated retrievals.
- Reject WMF payloads incorrectly published as enhanced metafiles.
- Restore mapped-format auto-conversion behavior.

## Test coverage

The branch adds exhaustive coverage for:

- Threading and apartment-state behavior.
- Argument validation and exception contracts.
- Text, audio, file-drop, bitmap, custom-format, and managed-object data.
- Windows-generated and managed format conversion.
- Clipboard ownership, replacement, persistence, and retries.
- Legacy and typed Clipboard APIs.
- Native EMF rendering, retrieval, mapping, streams, ownership, and disposal.
- EMF versus WMF validation.

Final validation:

- `PresentationCore.Tests`: 1,003 passed, 29 intentional skips, 0 failed.
- Clipboard tests: 65 passed, 4 intentional framework-difference skips, 0 failed.
- Repeated final runs completed without automatic retries or process crashes.

## Dependency

This requires the corresponding `System.Private.Windows.Core` changes from `dotnet/winforms`, including:

- Managed Clipboard owner lifetime fixes.
- Stale-owner and exited-STA handling.
- Platform-opted native Clipboard media.
- Shared `IDataObject` retry handling.
- Native EMF medium support and format enumeration.

For these changes we will need to update this PR with an updated version of `Microsoft.Private.WinForms` package once it is available.

Issues.Title: Fix completed WISP touch promotion across modal dialogs
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/wpf#2491 <!-- Issue Number -->

Main PR: Not applicable; this is the main-branch fix, not a backport. <!-- Link to PR if any that fixed this in the main branch. -->

## Description

<!-- Give a brief summary of the issue and how the pull request is fixing it. -->

Fix WISP touch-to-mouse promotion when a cancelled manipulation replays a mouse-down handler that synchronously opens a modal dialog.

With a panning ScrollViewer, a tap can be buffered until touch-up cancels manipulation. Replaying the buffered mouse down from inside touch-up can enter `ShowDialog()` before the original touch device deactivates. That device retains mouse-promotion ownership, preventing subsequent dialog touches from generating mouse events until WISP reuses its cursor ID. The reproduction on this machine ignored ten touches and first clicked on touch eleven; that count is device/environment dependent.

This change:

- Defers completed-touch cancellation replay until touch-up and deactivation finish, including cancellation triggered by capture release during deactivation. Handled `PreviewStylusUp` and `StylusUp` use the same completion scope without reporting a suppressed `TouchUp`. Mid-contact cancellation remains immediate.
- Detaches the replay queue and checks contact generations and queue revisions so reentrant callbacks cannot consume or clear newer input.
- Tracks the replay's actual mouse source and per-button ownership. Disabling or disposing that source retires only its still-owned press, without delivering a synthetic mouse-up to a disabled/disposed source.
- Resolves replay eligibility and press receipts across nested operations and prevents stale cached-down writes after outbound callbacks.
- Retires stale replay bookkeeping when real mouse input takes over its button, and tracks that affected button through physical release even after the replay returns. A held physical press survives old replay cleanup; source re-enable resynchronizes it from system state. Unrelated legacy mouse/stylus button handling is unchanged.

Adds 46 deterministic bookkeeping/ownership cases in `PresentationCore.Tests` and 14 opt-in native cases in `PresentationFramework.Tests`, plus the project references needed by the exercised input/UI paths.

The product change is WISP-only: no public API or pointer-stack changes. The separate non-panning, live-contact modal variant is outside this fix's scope.

Related: dotnet/wpf#194 and dotnet/wpf#11999. I also tested the unchanged native regressions with only the product patch from dotnet/wpf#11999 at `5f54e6051b42fa8f27ca1c1b5a67cdcc183570da`, on the same upstream baseline and without this PR's product changes. Its Release build improved the first successful dialog click from touch eleven to touch one, but still missed the Click on touch ten. A fresh process running only the three modal cases reproduced the same failure; both Click-based controls passed. Its full Release native suite had 9 passes and 3 failures (the modal case, handled-TouchUp completion, and throwing-handler recovery). Its Debug suite aborted on a WISP assertion during the modal case. This is evidence of overlapping behavior, not a claim that every scenario reported under the two issues is identical or that the other failures were introduced by that PR.

## Customer Impact

<!-- What is the impact to customers of not taking this fix? -->

Touch-operated applications opening modal dialogs from promoted mouse-down handlers can appear unresponsive: touch events reach the dialog, but Buttons and other mouse-dependent controls do not receive the corresponding mouse events. Customers may need repeated taps before controls start responding.

The regression verifies that every one of 36 dialog touches clicks across three open/close cycles, rather than checking only eventual recovery.

## Regression

<!-- Is this fixing a problem that was introduced in the most recent release, ie., fixing a regression? -->

No known recent-release regression. The issue is longstanding and has also been reported on .NET Framework.

## Testing

<!-- What kind of testing has been done with the fix. -->

Validated locally on Windows, x64 Debug, at commit `98a75a9bf310853d185635b75a86e1bdbb64a922`, based on upstream `5edf2b293`. Tests target `net11.0-windows` and ran on `.NET 12.0.0-alpha.1.26509.101`. The commands/results below were rerun after addressing the two review findings.

Before the corrections, seven new managed cases failed on the original PR product code: handled-preview-up deactivation, left/right physical press/release followed by another touch, and held physical-button cleanup. All pass after correction. Additional coverage checks release after the replay has left the active stack, nested left/right takeover, release without an observed press, and preservation of unrelated legacy button behavior.

Builds:

```powershell
$env:LC_ALL = 'C'; $env:LANG = 'C'; .\build.cmd -projects 'src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\tests\UnitTests\PresentationCore.Tests\PresentationCore.Tests.csproj' -platform x64 -msbuildEngine vs -verbosity quiet -binaryLogName Issue2491Review-PresentationCore.Tests.binlog
```

Result: **passed**, 0 warnings, 0 errors; exit 0.

```powershell
$env:LC_ALL = 'C'; $env:LANG = 'C'; .\build.cmd -projects 'src\Microsoft.DotNet.Wpf\tests\UnitTests\PresentationFramework.Tests\PresentationFramework.Tests.csproj' -platform x64 -msbuildEngine vs -verbosity quiet -binaryLogName Issue2491Review-PresentationFramework.Tests.binlog
```

Result: **passed**, 0 warnings, 0 errors; exit 0. Builds used existing installed tools/artifacts; clean-machine bootstrap is not validated.

Core input compatibility:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_ROOT = (Resolve-Path .dotnet).Path; & .\artifacts\bin\PresentationCore.Tests\x64\Debug\net11.0-windows\PresentationCore.Tests.exe --filter-class 'System.Windows.Input.*' --no-progress --report-xunit-xml --report-xunit-xml-filename Issue2491ReviewInput.xml --timeout 2m
```

Result: **249 passed**, 0 failed, 0 skipped; exit 0. Includes all 46 new WISP cases, including nested-operation coverage. These managed ownership/lifetime models are not physical-device tests.

Native desktop touch regressions:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_ROOT = (Resolve-Path .dotnet).Path; $env:WPF_TEST_DESKTOP_TOUCH = '1'; try { & .\artifacts\bin\PresentationFramework.Tests\x64\Debug\net11.0-windows\PresentationFramework.Tests.exe --filter-class System.Windows.Input.WispModalTouchTests --no-progress --report-xunit-xml --report-xunit-xml-filename Issue2491ReviewNative.xml --timeout 2m; $testExit = $LASTEXITCODE } finally { Remove-Item Env:WPF_TEST_DESKTOP_TOUCH }; exit $testExit
```

Result: **14 passed**, 0 failed, 0 skipped; exit 0. Covers the modal/control matrix, handled touch input, successful panning/inertia, mid-contact cancellation, source closure, throwing-handler recovery, simultaneous contacts, and cross-window mouse capture transfer. The two new modal cases handle `PreviewStylusUp` and `StylusUp`; both require deactivation before opening the dialog, no promoted `TouchUp`, and every one of 36 dialog touches clicking across three cycles.

This is guarded native touch injection on an explicitly idle interactive desktop. The tests assert locally loaded WPF assemblies and observed WISP touch devices; foreground, process-ownership and unobscured-window guards stay enabled. The modal regression failed before the fix with first successful dialog touch eleven and passes with this fix for every touch across all three cycles.

Default opt-in gating:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_ROOT = (Resolve-Path .dotnet).Path; if (Test-Path Env:WPF_TEST_DESKTOP_TOUCH) { Remove-Item Env:WPF_TEST_DESKTOP_TOUCH }; & .\artifacts\bin\PresentationFramework.Tests\x64\Debug\net11.0-windows\PresentationFramework.Tests.exe --filter-class System.Windows.Input.WispModalTouchTests --no-progress --report-xunit-xml --report-xunit-xml-filename Issue2491ReviewDefault.xml --timeout 1m
```

Result: **14 skipped**, 0 executed; expected all-skipped exit 8. Do not enable native injection on a shared/unattended desktop or run another desktop test executable concurrently.

```powershell

```

```powershell

```

Result: **passed**, exit 0. The staged review-correction diff was also checked with `git diff --cached --check`: passed.

**Pending / not run:** physical touch-device validation by a teammate; physical mouse/pen and monitor/DPI combinations; native nested contact reuse/hot-unplug and source closure specifically during a pre-press move; full OLE drag/drop resynchronization; pointer-stack runtime testing; the full repository suite. Targeted DRT binaries were unavailable, so DRTs were not run. The original non-panning live-contact variant was not revalidated on the final binaries.

## Risk

<!-- Please assess the risk of taking this fix. Provide details backing up your assessment. -->

**Medium.** This changes reentrant WISP touch-up/manipulation-cancellation ordering and shared mouse-state bookkeeping. The completed-touch path intentionally finishes touch-up and deactivation before replaying buffered mouse input.

Risk is constrained by leaving immediate mid-contact cancellation and the pointer implementation unchanged, checking source identity/contact generation/queue revision, and releasing only a provably owned mouse press. Deterministic and native tests cover nested operations, primary/secondary contacts, source lifetime and capture transfer, but do not replace hardware validation.

This PR is a **draft pending physical-device testing and review of the input-lifecycle changes**.

This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Crafted WPF pixel-shader bytecode can desynchronize the two parsing passes in `CPSTrans::Initialize`, causing heap out-of-bounds writes or reads. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/475 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. WPF XPS hyperlink navigation can bypass URI restrictions and reach an attacker-controlled `ObjectDataProvider`, enabling remote code execution after user interaction. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/456 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-358 (Improperly Implemented Security Check for Standard) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 | 8.0.32 [Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 | 8.0.32 [Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/wpf. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind.
